audience.text: Python developers building applications that need to generate, modify, or process PowerPoint presentations programmatically.

capabilities.text: Create new presentations and open existing .pptx files using `slides.Presentation` as a context manager, then save to various Office Open XML formats.
capabilities.title: Presentation creation and editing

capabilities.text: Add and format auto shapes, tables, connectors, groups, and picture frames; style text at portion, paragraph, and frame levels with bullets and font properties.
capabilities.title: Shape and text manipulation

capabilities.text: Insert 74 chart types backed by an embedded XLSX workbook, define series and categories, and configure titles, legends, data labels, and trendlines.
capabilities.title: Chart building

capabilities.text: Apply slide transitions with timing and advance settings, and create animation sequences with behaviors, motion paths, and triggers.
capabilities.title: Animations and transitions

capabilities.text: Apply solid, gradient, pattern, and picture fills to shapes and backgrounds; style lines with arrowheads and dash patterns; add shadow, glow, blur, reflection, and soft edge effects.
capabilities.title: Styling and effects

capabilities.text: Set built-in and custom document properties, add speaker notes with header/footer visibility control, and manage threaded comments with authors and positions.
capabilities.title: Document properties and notes

capabilities.text: Embed images from file handles or bytes using `Images.from_file`, `Images.from_stream`, or `ImageCollection.add_image`.
capabilities.title: Image embedding

capabilities.text: Export presentation text, tables, lists, headings, comments, and chart data to Markdown in 24 dialects via `SaveFormat.MD`.
capabilities.title: Markdown export

limitations.text: No rendering or conversion to PDF, HTML, XPS, or image formats is supported; the library only writes OOXML.
Reading is limited to .pptx; only specific save formats (Pptx, Pptm, Ppsx, Ppsm, Potx, Potm, MD) are supported, others raise ValueError.
SmartArt, OLE objects, mathematical text, VBA macros, and digital signatures are not implemented and raise NotImplementedError.
Presentation sections and slide size APIs are not exposed; new decks use the bundled template's 16:9 size.
Comment threads are written using the classic schema; modern thread features are not represented.
Action settings other than external hyperlinks are not implemented.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic PowerPoint file manipulation in Python without installing Microsoft Office or using COM interop.
Supports round-trip preservation of unknown XML parts in .pptx files during load and save operations.
Provides a native Python API to build presentations with shapes, text, tables, charts, images, animations, transitions, and speaker notes.

product_summary.text: Aspose.Slides FOSS for Python is an open-source Python library for creating, reading, and editing PowerPoint .pptx presentations without requiring Microsoft Office.

uncertainties: Whether the library supports saving to .pptm, .ppsx, .ppsm, .potx, and .potm formats beyond .pptx is implied but not explicitly confirmed by examples.
The exact set of SaveFormat values that raise ValueError at save time is not listed in the facts.
Whether TextAnimation.add_effect is the only explicitly stubbed method is not fully confirmed beyond the README claim.
The behavior when assigning to a non-existent property on a shape or formatting object is described in the README but not directly verified by examples.
Whether unknown XML parts are preserved verbatim on save for all possible unknown parts is not exhaustively tested in the examples.
The exact Python version support beyond 3.10-3.14 is not specified in the facts.
Whether the library supports reading or writing .ppt (legacy PowerPoint format) is not confirmed.
The exact set of public symbols that raise NotImplementedError is not fully listed in the facts.

workflows.name: Open and save presentations
workflows.text: Use `slides.Presentation` as a context manager to open an existing .pptx file and save it, optionally with a different format.

workflows.name: Add shapes and text
workflows.text: Create new presentations, access the first slide, add auto shapes, and insert text frames with formatted content.

workflows.name: Embed images
workflows.text: Load images from file handles or bytes and add them as picture frames to slides.

workflows.name: Build charts
workflows.text: Add charts with embedded workbooks, define series and categories, and populate data points.

workflows.name: Apply slide transitions
workflows.text: Set transition types, timing, and click advance for slides using `slide_show_transition`.

workflows.name: Run tests
workflows.text: Execute the test suite using `python -m pytest -q` on Python 3.10 through 3.14 across Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS.
